origin: Like a ship that stays near where it drops anchor, people judge near the first number they see. Amos Tversky and Daniel Kahneman introduced it in 1974.
whenToUse: You show the price before discount or a comparison price.
You set the order of plans.
You review the honesty of price displays.
whenNotToUse: You'd show an inflated list price the product never sold at.
You'd hide the source of the reference price.
The comparison is with a different product.

alternatives.name: Strikethrough Price
alternatives.reason: Showing prices before and after a discount.

alternatives.name: Decoy Effect
alternatives.reason: When the lineup of options changes judgment.

accessibility: Label the struck-through price as the list price so its meaning comes through to screen readers too.
Write the discount amount in words.
Don't convey meaning with color and strikethrough alone.
